The candidate demonstrated a strong overall grasp of financial calculations in Item 1, effectively performing multi-step operations to determine phased revenues, expense totals, and member profit shares. The candidate's strongest performance appeared in Item 1 Part (a), where they accurately calculated the bag quantities and revenues across all three sales phases—such as obtaining 701.4 bags at UGX 100,000 to yield UGX 70,140,000 for Phase 2—and correctly calculated the flat-rate comparison revenue of UGX 102,000,000 in Part (b). Conversely, the candidate's main weakness lies in coordinate geometry area determination in Item 2 Part (a), where they attempted a corrupted version of Heron's formula with additive terms inside the radical, arriving at an erroneous area of 141.6 square meters instead of using the straightforward base-height approach. A secondary observation is that while the candidate successfully applied follow-through logic in Item 2 Part (b) to determine material quantities and correctly calculated the overall budget of UGX 750,000, they omitted the explicit weighted average price per bag calculation in Item 1 Part (b) and left the qualitative justification for rounding up unfinished. Furthermore, minor arithmetic slips occurred, such as subtracting four million from total revenue to get UGX 101,353,000 instead of 101,352,000. To improve, the candidate should practice using simple perpendicular base-height methods for right or aligned triangles on coordinate grids to prevent unnecessary formula errors, and ensure all written analytical responses include full, completed explanatory sentences and required formal reporting headers.
